title: WWE Isn't a Wrestling Company

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: SummerSlam looks like a wrestling show. [exhales] It's actually a streaming product now — and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Follow the money. Netflix pays five billion over ten years — Raw's the crown jewel. ESPN pays another one-point-six billion just for the big events, like SummerSlam.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: Media money is now fifty-nine percent of everything WWE makes. Tickets? Twenty-four. The show in the arena is basically a TV set.

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: And it's working. Last year WWE out-earned UFC — one-point-seven billion to one-point-five. First time since they merged under TKO.

viz.stamp: FIRST TIME IN THE TKO ERA

lines.speaker: george
lines.text: So this weekend, watch SummerSlam like an investor. Every big moment is built to travel — a clip, a thumbnail, a reason to subscribe. That's the real match.

viz.sub: EVERY MOMENT IS BUILT TO TRAVEL.

caption: SummerSlam looks like wrestling. It's actually a streaming product — $5B from Netflix, $1.6B from ESPN, and the first year WWE out-earned UFC. Watch it like an investor.
